HEDGE FUNDS DUMP TECH STOCKS AT FASTEST PACE IN A DECADE Goldman Sachs reports that hedge funds cut technology exposure at the fastest pace since at least 2016 during the five sessions ending October 15. The Nasdaq 100 plunged 5.5% last week, while semiconductor stocks suffered the largest dollar selling. Despite the selloff, tech still represents 23.5% of hedge fund portfolios, near historically elevated levels.

GOLDMAN SACHS: U.S. GDP HOLDS STRONG DESPITE HOUSING SLUMP U.S. housing starts plunged 5.2% in September to 1.221 million, missing expectations. Single-family starts fell 4.6%, multifamily starts dropped 6.7%, and building permits slipped 0.2%. Despite the weakness, Goldman Sachs maintained its Q3 GDP growth estimate at 3.3% annualized.

U.S. PENDING HOME SALES PLUNGE 7.3% IN SEPTEMBER U.S. pending home sales fell 7.3% month-over-month in September, reversing August's modest 0.3% gain. The index dropped to 66.0, with sales down 11.3% year-over-year. All four regions weakened, led by the West (-9.2%) and South (-8.2%).
